version.value: Complete first movement of the orchestral symphony
version.note: The Archive item lists the four movements and splits the set into three files without saying which file holds which movement. The first file runs 8 min 2 s and ends in a quiet close that matches Hyperion’s description of the first movement’s pianissimo coda.

performers.note: Both the Archive item and the EMI reissue notes credit the composer as conductor. Individual players are not identified.

date.note: The Archive item writes the date as 11-10-1937; the EMI reissue notes give 11th October 1937.

place.note: The EMI reissue notes name No. 1 Studio, Abbey Road; BBC Music Magazine places the session in Abbey Road Studio 1.

catalogue.note: The Archive item catalogues the set as DB 8406–9 (automatic coupling); the EMI reissue notes give DB 3367–3370 as the original 78s. They probably label the same performances in two side sequences, but that is not established here.

matrixTakeSides.note: The Archive description lists the takes; the EMI notes list the same matrix numbers. Which sides make up the first file is not stated.

credits.note: The item is filed in that collection; no transfer engineer is named in the description.

date.note: The Archive upload date (13 May 2018) is not a transfer date.

processing.value: FLAC, Ogg Vorbis and variable-bitrate MP3 derivatives, in three segments (a first file, a second, and a third joining the remaining two discs).
processing.note: Equalisation, speed correction and noise reduction are not documented.

digital.format: VBR MP3 derivative of a 78-rpm transfer

composition.value: Vaughan Williams’s copyright in the music runs to the end of 2028 in the UK and EU.
composition.note: The Vaughan Williams Foundation gives 2028 as the year copyright in his music expires. Composition rights are separate from the recording.

recording.value: Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial issue in 1938, before 1963
recording.note: The EMI reissue notes date the original HMV 78s “℗ 1938”. The project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule then applies: the former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is not United States or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

rights.creditLine: Ralph Vaughan Williams, Symphony No. 4, I. Allegro; BBC Symphony Orchestra, Ralph Vaughan Williams. HMV DB 8406–9 (first issued 1938), Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; Vaughan Williams’s copyright subsists in the UK and EU until the end of 2028.
